dedupe_keys.name: ofr financial stress index ofr fsi

description: The OFR Financial Stress Index is a daily market-based snapshot of stress in global financial markets, published by the U.S. Office of Financial Research. It is built from 33 financial market variables, such as yield spreads, valuation measures and interest rates, grouped into five categories (credit, equity valuation, funding, safe assets and volatility), and shows stress contributions from three regions: the United States, other advanced economies and emerging markets. A statistical algorithm weights the variables by how they move together; the index is positive when stress is above average and negative when below. Data are current to two business days before publication. The page offers line and column charts by category and region and a download of all data, free of charge; no licence is stated on the page. A notice records a corrected data-feed error for May 2026. Caveats: it measures market stress, not operational disruption. For simulation it gives a daily stress signal for financial-sector scenarios and for linking market stress to infrastructure shocks and events. Related catalogue records include the OFR Bank Systemic Risk Monitor and NYU V-Lab SRISK.
